question: Which antigen of Salmonella Typhi is a polysaccharide capsular virulence factor used as the basis for both the injectable typhoid vaccine and the chronic carrier screening test?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Vi (virulence) antigen is a capsular polysaccharide unique to S. Typhi. It inhibits phagocytosis and complement-mediated killing. The Vi polysaccharide vaccine (e.g. Typhim Vi) targets this antigen, and elevated Vi agglutination titres (≥1:20) help screen for chronic biliary carriers.

Incorrect. The O antigen is the somatic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) cell wall antigen detected in the Widal test. A rising O titre indicates active infection, but it is not the basis of the carrier screening test or the polysaccharide vaccine.

Incorrect. The H antigen is the flagellar protein antigen. Elevated H titres in the Widal test suggest past infection or prior TAB vaccination. It is not a capsular virulence factor and is not used for carrier screening.
Incorrect. K antigens are capsular antigens found in other Enterobacteriaceae (e.g. E. coli K1). The capsular antigen of S. Typhi is specifically designated the Vi antigen, not K.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the three Salmonella antigens: O (somatic/LPS — Widal, active infection), H (flagellar — Widal, past infection/vaccination), Vi (capsular — virulence, vaccine, carrier screening). Vi is unique to S. Typhi.

The Vi antigen serves three high-yield functions: (1) virulence factor inhibiting phagocytosis, (2) target of the injectable polysaccharide vaccine, and (3) marker for chronic biliary carrier screening (Vi agglutination ≥1:20).
